(1) The 2016 MARAD/USCG Final EIS for Port Delfin (https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2018/11/f57/final-eis-0531-port-delfin-lng-main-volume-2016-11.pdf) states: 'one 700-ft, 42-inch-diameter bypass around existing West Cameron block 167 (WC 167) offshore manifold platform' interconnecting the former UTOS and HIOS pipelines; its own summary table gives Length 700 feet/213 meters and Diameter 42 inches/107 cm for this exact bypass. (2) Delfin's own March 1, 2024 DOE/FECM extension-request filing (https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-03/Delfin%20DOE%20Extension%20request%20(030124%20FINAL).pdf, Docket Nos. 13-129-LNG/13-147-LNG) independently describes 'a new offshore pipeline to interconnect UTOS and HIOS, bypassing the platform where they currently connect,' citing the MARAD Record of Decision. The July 29, 2015 Federal Register deepwater-port-license-application notice (2015-18594) and a contemporaneous May 11, 2015 oedigital.com article independently corroborate the original proposal and existence of the project this pipeline belongs to.
CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified transmission -- an interconnection bypass between two historically FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission systems (UTOS, HIOS), not a gathering/feeder line. Fuel=Gas confirmed by the EIS.
DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any of the other 43 roster rows. It is the unique 700-ft/0.21 km, 42-in WC167 bypass; distinct from the four ~30-in, ~6,400-ft laterals running from HIOS to each FLNGV and from the ~0.25-mile onshore supply-header pipeline described in the same EIS -- neither of those is a separate row in this batch, so no merge/relabel action is needed.

resolutions.recommendation: reclassify PipelineType from 'transmission' to 'gathering' -- FERC's own jurisdictional ruling on this exact system
resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's current PipelineType='transmission' is supported only by a citation to eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines, a navigation page that does not name this pipeline (builder's own relevance check: name_found=false) -- so the value was effectively uncited, not merely under-cited. Independent, on-point evidence says the opposite: on 2024-09-27 FERC issued an Order on Petition for Order to Show Cause (Energy Transfer LP's petition, docket proceedings around CP24-122) applying the 'primary function test' and finding the LEG System -- despite its large 30-42in diameter and high operating pressure, both typical of transmission -- is legally and functionally a GATHERING system: a spine-like configuration gathering unprocessed gas from ~775 wellhead receipt points along its length, with no FERC NGA jurisdiction. Reported independently by a law firm (Van Ness Feldman, via natlawreview.com) and by trade press (naturalgasintel.com, 'Williams Prevails as FERC Rules Louisiana LEG System a Natural Gas Gathering Pipe'), both describing the same primary document with matching specifics (174 mi, 1.8 Bcf/d, 775 receipt points). Williams' own SEC 10-Qs likewise describe LEG only as 'natural gas gathering assets' / 'gathering system', never as an interstate transmission line. `gathering` is a valid value in the repo's controlled vocabulary (docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md). This is a genuine misclassification, not a close call -- FERC's order is a formal jurisdictional determination on this exact system.
